utterances.speaker: BORISLAVA DAKIC
utterances.text: Well, it's easy because we, in the former Yugoslavia, probably didn't have the same kind of system as you did. It may sound strange to you that I should know this. But as I told you, the medical centre was an umbrella organisation which consisted of several components which I have already enumerated. Out patients' clinics, hospitals, pharmacies, and other such institutions. The overall health care was provided by the medical centre. When the war activity started in the area of Prijedor Municipality, and when the law on associated labour ceased to apply in the territory of the former republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the medical centre became one single unit. The Sanski Most outpatients' clinic and the Sanski Most pharmacy were no longer part of the medical centre. They were not in the territory of Prijedor Municipality. They belonged to a separate municipality. So as of 1992, it was the Prijedor's outpatients' clinic, Prijedor pharmacy, and the occupational medicine centre were part of the Prijedor medical centre.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Pause there, please. Were you privy to any documentation or files in relation to these dates?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAVA DAKIC
utterances.text: Yes. In May 1992 [as interpreted], the Municipal Assembly sent a decision to the medical centre whereby Dr. Milan Kovacevic was appointed chief of medical centre, and Dr. Milomir Stakic his deputy. So the two of them remained in these offices until the end of 1994. In the course of 1994, the assembly of Republika Srpska adopted a new law on health care whereby it established the overall network of health institutions in the republic. This law provided for the existence of separate hospitals, clinical centres, outpatients' clinic, and so on and so forth. These institutions became separate. Thereby, a reorganisation was done as far as health care is concerned. This was done in Banja Luka in respect of our area. So I was also involved in the implementation of this new law, law on health care. I took the documentation to the Court, and I know that the court issued a decision whereby the outpatients' clinic started to exist as a separate institution on the 1st of January, 1995. On that day, the hospital became an independent medical institution, and the Novi Grad outpatients' clinic, the Prijedor pharmacy, they all became independent, separate medical institutions. And that is why I clearly remember these dates. And that's why I know on that day, as a result of this reorganisation, the Municipal Assembly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sorry, I want to correct something what may be reflected not correctly on page 46, line 2. Here is reads: In May 1992, the Municipal Assembly sent a decision to the medical centre whereby Milan Kovacevic was appointed and so on. I think -- is it true you wanted to say 1992, or did you say 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1993, yes, yes, 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So if this could be please corrected. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I was just about to clear that up.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mrs. Dakic, how do you remember the date of the 19th of May, 1993, as the date Dr. Stakic became deputy of the health centre?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAVA DAKIC
utterances.text: I will tell you how it happened. As of May 1992, the office of the director of the medical centre was held by Ranko Sikman. In May 1993, the information that the Prijedor medical centre director, Mr. Ranko Sikman, reached me in the afternoon hours on that day as I was sitting on a bench in front of my house. Because a deputy of the Prijedor Municipal Assembly, whom I knew, happened to pass by, and in an informal conversation, he told me as a worker of a medical centre: "Well, today, we have dismissed Sikman, and we are giving Stakic and Kovacevic back to you." Several days later, a written decision to that effect arrived; that is, the appointment of Mr. Kovacevic to the office of the director. Because Mr. Kovacevic was also one of our physicians who came to occupy an office, that is, the office of the president of the executive council after the multiparty elections, this decision had to be entered into the proper records, which I still have because such changes need to be kept. I also have a decision on the appointment of Dr. Stakic as chief of outpatients' clinic, and all these decisions are part of the appropriate records that I still keep.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Can you tell us the date Dr. Stakic stopped being the chief executive officer of the medical centre?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAVA DAKIC
utterances.text: The 16th of July, 1988, it was Dr. Spomenka Pavkovic who was appointed to that position. Her mandate has been renewed recently as a director.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'm sorry. In the transcript, your answer reads "the 16th of July, 1988." Can you clarify the date for the Court, please.

utterances.speaker: BORISLAVA DAKIC
utterances.text: Dr. Stakic, while he was director of the medical centre, head medical centre, applied to be sent to specialisation in physiotherapy. In 1995/1996, he was still director of the medical centre, but was also head of the Prijedor Municipality. These two functions can theoretically coexist, but they require a considerable amount of effort. And he appointed --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, we missed the last part of the witness's answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could you pause there for a moment. Two things to follow up your answer. My question was very simple. In your last answer, when I asked you to tell us the date Dr. Stakic stopped being the chief executive officer of the medical centre, your answer in the transcript is the 16th of July, 1988. Can you please clarify the year that he left.

utterances.speaker: BORISLAVA DAKIC
utterances.text: He was the director of the medical centre until that time, and he was assisted in his work by his deputies.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If Dr. Stakic was appointed as chief executive officer of the health centre on the 1st of January, 1995, what year did he cease as chief executive officer? Was it 1997 or 1998? Because the transcript reads "1988."

utterances.speaker: BORISLAVA DAKIC
utterances.text: In 1998. I'm afraid I have misunderstood your question. I must have made a mistake in the year. That's why I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Dr. Stakic stopped coming to work days after the arrest of Dr. Kovacevic on the 10th of July, 1997. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAVA DAKIC
utterances.text: Dr. Stakic did not come to work to the medical centre during 1996. I told you because of the workload in his capacity as the president of the municipality, he appointed Dr. Zeljko Macura to replace him. And I believe that the two of them consulted on the medical centre affairs. According to the records that we maintain at the medical centre, Dr. Stakic in 1997 left to complete his residency in Belgrade, and he sent us the reports on his residency because that residency had been granted to him long before that. And if he hadn't taken it at that time, the ministry of health would have withdrawn this permission. So this grant, residency grant, was time barred, so he had to take it at the time. That means, he didn't come to the medical centre physically, but according to us, and based on what I have told you, we did not consider that he had left work. All of our doctors who go for residency have to submit the letters of the institutions where they are sent to complete their residency. And that's what they do in order to prove to us that they are indeed doing what they have been sent to do.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: You mentioned that you had these previous decisions that we've talked about, his appointment on the 19th of May, 1993, and the 1st January, 1995. Do you also have the decision Dr. Zeljko Macura replaced him in 1996 in your file?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAVA DAKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Do you have the piece of paper in relation to his residency in Belgrade on your file?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAVA DAKIC
utterances.text: In the accounting department in the medical centre, there must be such a document. Otherwise, he could not have been paid for that period of time.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Do you know whether Dr. Stakic is still on the payroll of the Prijedor medical centre?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAVA DAKIC
utterances.text: Yes, he is. According to the provisions of the law on employment or the labour law, an employee against whom a legal procedure has been initiated is entitled to receive 50 per cent of his salary for the duration of that procedure, or for six months, or until the end of that procedure if the employer so decides. The CEO of the medical centre, in keeping with the provisions of this law, has decided to pay this small amount of money to Dr. Stakic. And whether this is going to be paid out until the moment a valid decision is made by this Honourable Court, I can't tell you. It really depends on the decision of my director. That is, of the director of the medical centre. It is possible, according to the labour law, for the director of the medical centre to say either tomorrow or the day after or next month that this remuneration will stop being paid. But for the first six months after the procedure was started, our institution was under the obligation to pay this money to Dr. Stakic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: After Dr. Stakic completed his residency that he left for in, you think, 1997 or 1998, did he return to work at the Prijedor medical centre or hospital?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAVA DAKIC
utterances.text: No, he did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And by his decision in 1996, he was replaced by Dr. Zeljko Macura. So from that point in 1996, he was no longer an employee of the medical centre or the hospital. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAVA DAKIC
utterances.text: No, it is not. It isn't. The deputy is appointed by the director. It is the director's decision. The director appoints the person who will sit in his place during his absence. And such a decision by the director does not immediately result in his termination of employment because he was appointed president of the municipality. Maybe this word "deputy" has confused you. It is not a deputy, it is the assistant director who acts on behalf of the director during the director's absence for justified reasons. If the Municipal Assembly of Prijedor had appointed Dr. Macura by the same decision, it would have relieved Dr. Stakic of his duties.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Do you know a person -- have you obtained any records from the hospital or the medical centre in relation to Dr. Stakic's defence?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAVA DAKIC
utterances.text: I'm afraid I don't understand your question, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Have you provided the Defence with any hospital records of any patients?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAVA DAKIC
utterances.text: Yes. When Trial Chamber or Prosecution has a case, they often approach us with a request to get an insight into the documentation of our patient who is at the same time the person being tried or charged with crimes. In October or November last year, that is, 2002, the Defence team of Dr. Stakic approached the medical centre, that is, the director of our medical centre, with a request to provide for the purposes of this Trial Chamber the medical chart testifying to the health condition of Mr. Nusret Sivac. I believe that is the gentleman's name. On director's order, the service where such documentation is kept has located the medical documentation of this person, and I believe that this documentation was delivered to the office for the cooperation with The Hague Tribunal, and that in turn, that a copy of that document has been delivered to Dr. Stakic's Defence team.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Along this line of questioning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Madam, I would like you to look at a document. While that's being distributed, could you please tell the Court the name of the director of the hospital, or the medical centre, who ordered that the records be Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. delivered up.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Excuse me, usher, before that's given to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Madam, could you tell me the name of the director of the Prijedor medical centre, please.

utterances.speaker: BORISLAVA DAKIC
utterances.text: Yes. Spomenka Pavkovic-Sekulic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Isn't it correct that within the meaning -- I'm sorry. I will begin my question again. Information about the state of health of a patient and about the causes, circumstances, and consequences of that state would be construed as a medical secret, would it not?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAVA DAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And isn't it correct that information of this nature may not be disclosed to other persons or published in a manner which would reveal the identity of the patient that that information pertains to?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAVA DAKIC
utterances.text: I've already told you, it is our practice that the director can approve the delivery of such information when a request comes either from the Prosecution or the basic court in Prijedor, all with the purpose of establishing the truth. It has happened on a number of occasions so far. In this particular case, it was the Defence team that has sent us such a request. I believe that my director believed that this carries the same weight as if it had been requested by the Prosecution. I'm not claiming that we have not made a mistake, but this has been the practice in our relationship with the judiciary system. Maybe in this case, we have not been vigilant enough. Maybe we have not had the right instructions, and maybe the director of the medical centre has indeed made a mistake in issuing an approval for such a document to be delivered to a third party.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, may we take an early break. You wanted to break at quarter to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think -- how long will it take you to continue with the line of questions on this issue?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was going to move on to another topic, unless you wanted me to continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Then please understand that before we move over to another issue, I want to ask the witness in person. Did you yourself give any legal advice to the person you just mentioned who ordered the handing out of this document? Was there any discussion on the legality and the question whether or not to hand over this document on the witness in this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I have not provided any advice, but I have told you that this is customary. This is what the procedure is. So my director did not even deem it necessary to ask for my advice, because this is part of our practice. And this was not the first time that somebody sent us a similar request. Maybe our judgement was wrong when we thought that the Trial Chamber, the Prosecution, and Defence are one and the same. Because maybe we were not aware of who has the right to ask for something, who is entitled to request something. But I believe that my director was guided by the former practice, and that she thought that it would not be a problem if we delivered this document to members of the legal profession. And she did that. Maybe it is our mistake; maybe we did not act correctly. It may be the case that the Defence is not entitled to the same thing as other members or parts of the judiciary system.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Do I understand you correctly that you in person were approached by the Defence team?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. The Defence team sent a letter to the medical centre. They issued a written request. All the letters that arrive at the address of the medical centre are opened by the personal assistant of the director. Since the director and myself work in the adjacent offices, and since this was relative to Dr. Stakic who had been our director and our employee, obviously the director showed me the letter with the request. So that's why I saw the letter. But I was not requested to give her any advice, nor was I in the position to give her any advice. Even if anybody had asked me for advice, to be honest, I would have acted as we had in the case when such a case arrived from the basic court in Prijedor. So I would have acted along the similar lines. I would not have seen any hidden agenda in that, and I would have thought that the procedure to be followed was the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: We are aware that you have an excellent recollection as regards time and persons. Do you, to the best of your recollection, can testify about who signed this request and when did the request arrive?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That request arrived while I was absent, and it was brought by somebody from Dr. Stakic's Defence team. I believe that it was one of his counsels. I am not in a position to tell you exactly who it was, but in any case, it was on behalf of the Defence team.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Whenever in your country a Defence team would, in a case pending in Republika Srpska, approach you and asking you to hand over documents which are protected under Article 13 of the law on protection of health, would you hand over these documents to a Defence team without any consent given by a judge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Until this case, we never had a case of a Defence team requesting something like that. All the requests came from the basic court in Prijedor or in Banja Luka, or the Prosecution. And this time, when the request arrived from the Defence team, we simply that this is what we were supposed to do and that we were dealing with one and the same thing, that required the same procedure in order to arrive at the truth. And believe me, not for a single moment did we think that we were making a mistake. In practice, so far, no Defence counsel acting on behalf of anybody in a case pending in our state has ever approached us with such a request, or at least I don't know of any such case in our practice so far.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: A final question before the break: Were you requested to hand over the entire dossier relevant to this concrete person, or were you asked to concentrate on a concrete period of time only?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the letter that I saw, that I cannot quote precisely, we were asked to provide the documents relevant to the health condition of Mr. Sivac; to be more precise, in respect of his eyesight. Since this is beyond my scope of authority, I did not work on that. It was done by our service which maintains records on our patients, including Mr. Sivac. They must have located his file, and I don't really know what it says in this file. That particular service must have delivered a document to the director without thinking twice on what it says in the document. And a nurse is not in the position to interpret a medical file; I am not in a position to do that. So they just delivered document, the file to the director, and that's that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. The trial stays adjourned until 5 minutes past 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please be seated. You may proceed immediately. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mrs. Dakic, was Dr. Stakic an efficient chief executive officer at the medical centre?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAVA DAKIC
utterances.text: Well, it's difficult to talk about it now, because in the period of time where Dr. Stakic was chief executive officer, the times were very difficult. We had almost nothing, and Dr. Stakic did his best in order to maintain the highest level possible at that time of health care. I don't know what exactly you mean when you say "an efficient chief executive officer." I mean, the centre did provide health care to all citizens of Prijedor Municipality, all outpatients' clinic were operational. We transported the sick to the hospital. If that's what you have in mind, then yes, he can be described as efficient.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: For example, did he keep himself informed of important events that were happening in the hospital, in the medical centre?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAVA DAKIC
utterances.text: Yes. Well, his main concern was to provide adequate health care to the patients, to have adequate medical equipment, the sanitary supplies, bandages, syringes, and the like, and also to make sure that in the small outpatients' clinics located in the neighbouring town, a doctor, a physician, is sent. That is the responsibility of the health centre, and that is what the chief of health centre was supposed to take care of.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Are you aware of whether Dr. Stakic visited the clinics and the infirmaries?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAVA DAKIC
utterances.text: You mean, in his capacity as the director?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: BORISLAVA DAKIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mrs. Dakic, the transcript unclear. Earlier, you testified in May without specifying a year you had meetings with Dr. Stakic about collecting firewood and sending ambulances to different places. Are you referring to May 1993?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAVA DAKIC
utterances.text: Yes, before that, I had never met with Dr. Stakic. Up until the time when he became the president of the municipality, he did not have any contacts with me until he became the chief of medical centre. As for conversations with Dr. Stakic in general, they were never personal. They were never of a private nature. Sometimes I attended these work meetings when my services were needed, and the subject was usually the current needs of the medical centre, later health centre, and individual medical units. And I attended these meetings only upon invitation.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I want to move to another topic. In 1992, were you a member of any political party?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAVA DAKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: What is your ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAVA DAKIC
utterances.text: Serb.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: You testified earlier that Dr. Stakic was a member of the radical party and that that was closer to you. What did you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAVA DAKIC
utterances.text: Rallies or meetings organised by the radical party led by Mr. Guberina -- I don't know whether it was a committee or a small cell that they had in the territory of Omarska -- took place some hundred metres away from my house, and I was able to watch who gathered there from the window of my house. And I knew that the meeting in question was some kind of founding assembly, a founding rally. Later from the people who were present there, I heard that Mr. Stakic had been elected president. And the local board or whatever it was called -- I never made any effort to learn what it was called, however this organisational unit, whether it was in charge of Prijedor or Omarska, I don't know, but it was all in connection with this radical party which was organised and led by Mr. Veljko Guberina.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I want to move on to another topic, and I wish to show you a number of documents. But before I do that, you stated in your evidence that between the 28th of April and the 3rd of May, 1992, everything remained the same, and that no one had been sacked. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAVA DAKIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is, except for the cases of disciplinary proceedings or in accordance with the law that is still applicable. I did not notice anything of that kind happening at the time, nor did I observe any such thing in my department. I never saw my boss call any of the employees to his office for that purpose. We normally came to work, we normally talked, and I can claim that during that period of time, there were no dismissals, which doesn't mean, again, that this measure of termination of employment was not imposed in respect of someone who had broken some rules. But that practice had nothing to do with the events taking place at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The date, was it -- did I understand correctly you were referring to the 28th of April to the 3rd of May, or were you referring from the 28th of April or to the 30th of May?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAVA DAKIC
utterances.text: No, not to the 30th of May; I said explicitly during the period of time which is linked to the so-called takeover in the territory of Prijedor Municipality. During those several days, in my view, then and now, everything was the same as it was on the 27th. Nothing in particular happened, although the tension was visible at the time, I agree. But there were no -- any particular events that would merit any special comment.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Isn't it correct a number of persons were dismissed from the posts of directors of socially-owned companies during May 1992, after the takeover, shortly after the takeover?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAVA DAKIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct that directors of individual companies were replaced or dismissed. But I couldn't tell you the names of these people because at the medical centre, the director was appointed because the managing organ, the managing board which, until then, had performed that function, ceased to exist. So I cannot tell you the names of previous directors and who was appointed, if anyone afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Leaving the hospital aside for one moment, are you aware and isn't it correct that a number of Muslims and Croats were dismissed from their positions as directors of companies and were replaced by persons of Serb ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAVA DAKIC
utterances.text: That was not the case with the medical centre. In 1992 --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Pause there, please. I said leaving the hospital and the medical centre aside, aren't you aware and isn't that correct that a number of Muslim and Croat directors were dismissed from their employment as directors of companies and replaced by people of Serb ethnicity shortly after the takeover in May 1992?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAVA DAKIC
utterances.text: This is probably true because a large number of Muslim residents had left the territory of Prijedor, so probably one of the persons who held the office of the director also left. In view of the fact that it was mostly the Serb population that remained in the territory of the municipality, it is only reasonable to conclude that most of them were Serb. But I was not particularly knowledgeable about these things at the time. I don't know when these people left and who replaced them in their respective offices, the offices of directors.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I ask you, in between that we maybe can take Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. the necessary measures, do you regard it also as "leaving the territory" when a person was arrested in Omarska and Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When I said "leaving the territory," I meant the people who had moved outside the territory of Prijedor Municipality and took residence someplace else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And what about others?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To my understanding, they didn't leave Prijedor Municipality. At the time, they were still there. If someone was arrested and detained in the territory of Prijedor Municipality, then it means that he or she was still there but was probably prevented from performing their duties. If their freedom of movement was restricted, then obviously they couldn't come to work. This is a very simple conclusion that I'm able to reach.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes, but you're a lawyer by profession. Would you regard it as a reason if a person is arrested in a camp for, say, as you mentioned, more than five days, would you regard this as a reason for dismissal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, personally I wouldn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please continue with your line of questions. And feel free to ask for, if necessary, admonition on the Rule 91.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mrs. Dakic, as a lawyer, do you know a former colleague Esad Mehmedagic, a former legal colleague?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAVA DAKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Do you know a person called Slobodan Radulj?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAVA DAKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I would ask you to look at the following document which is Rule 65 ter number -- I'm sorry, it's an exhibit. S25.

utterances.speaker: BORISLAVA DAKIC
utterances.text: Please, I see here a different name. You asked me if I knew the person by the name Slobodan Radzo. Here in the transcript, I can read Slobodan Radulj.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Do you know this person?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAVA DAKIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: What is his ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAVA DAKIC
utterances.text: Serb.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Looking at Exhibit S25, if the English translation could be placed on the ELMO machine, you spoke a moment ago about people, directors, and other persons being dismissed from employment because they left the territory. Do you know what happened to Esad Mehmedagic, the man who was dismissed from the post of municipal public attorney? Do you know that he was taken to the Omarska camp after the attack on Prijedor on the 30th of May, 1992, and that he disappeared from the Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAVA DAKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: This gentleman had very, very bad eyesight and was nearly blind. Does that remind you at all of who this person is?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAVA DAKIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't know any of these people.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Looking at S25, which is a decision of the 4th of May, 1992, of the executive committee of the Serbian Municipality of Prijedor, in fact it dismisses Esad Mehmedagic and appoints Slobodan Radulj. What is Slobodan's Radulj's ethnicity, if you know?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAVA DAKIC
utterances.text: Serb.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And do you know the ethnicity of Esad Mehmedagic?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAVA DAKIC
utterances.text: I do. Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I've finished with that document.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Do you know a man by the name of Nedzad Seric?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAVA DAKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Who was the presiding judge of the municipal court in Prijedor in 1992, in April 1992?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAVA DAKIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Do you know who was president of the elections commission during the March 1992 elections?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAVA DAKIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Mrs. Dakic --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the presiding judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. We are extremely grateful that today, on the basis of your testimony, we got a more close view on the CV of Dr. Stakic. May I therefore start with this question: You mentioned that on the 19th of May, 1993, he became deputy chief executive officer of the health centre, the same date Dr. Milan Kovacevic was chief. Do you know as not in your professional capacity but as a citizen of the municipality of Prijedor, what were the reasons why both of them at the same time moved from the political area back to the health area?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAVA DAKIC
utterances.text: I think it was for the following reason: They were relieved of their respective duties, that is, of the vice-president of the municipality and the president of the executive board. And since they were both persons who joined politics from the health centre, it was only normal for them to return to the institutions from which they originally came. It was simply a practice for the people who joined political life, once they are through with it, to return to their original duties, not only in the health centre but in any other company.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: But do you know something about the reasons why they had together to leave the political field?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAVA DAKIC
utterances.text: No, I don't. Rumour had it at the time that Dr. Stakic more often than Dr. Kovacevic was not a suitable for the duties of the president of the Municipal Assembly. But this was just a rumour; this was something that was heard on the grapevine. I never heard it said officially at a meeting, a rally, or I never heard it coming from an official source.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And to go furthermore in one detail, you mentioned that Dr. Stakic remained in this capacity until the end of 1994, and then became the 1st of January, 1995, the director of the health centre. To the best of your recollection, he really remained there until the end of 1994? Or was there any gap for what reason soever in 1994?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAVA DAKIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, there were no changes on the part of the organ who appointed Dr. Stakic as deputy CEO. During 1994, the Municipal Assembly of Prijedor made a decision on organising the health centre as an independent institution and appointed Dr. Stakic as its director which was then delivered, together with other documents, to the registration court in Banja Luka. Whether anything happened in the meantime, I don't know. I wouldn't be able to tell you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Was there maybe a de facto interruption of his work in 1994? Because we have to find out the truth, and we heard slightly different evidence in the past, but only if you know, of course.

utterances.speaker: BORISLAVA DAKIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Did you prepare today's testimony by revisiting your documents on Dr. Stakic, which would be quite normal, if not the duty of a witness?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAVA DAKIC
utterances.text: The facts that I presented before this Honourable Chamber today are the facts that I knew the very moment I was informed that I might be invited to appear as a witness before this Chamber. All the events that took place during 1992 were extremely bad and are of such nature that I'm sure I will remember for a long time. You simply don't forget such things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Did you take ever copies of the file of Dr. Stakic?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAVA DAKIC
utterances.text: No, not me. What copies of files do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Previously in your testimony you told us that as usual in the administration, one could find all the letters on the appointment of Dr. Stakic and so on. So therefore, I think there must be a kind of file where we could find these documents. And my question was related to this. Did you ever take or ask anybody to provide you with copies of this file in whole or in part?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAVA DAKIC
utterances.text: No, I've never requested anything. When Dr. Stakic was appointed director, we received in the mail from the competent organ that had appointed him a relevant decision which said that Dr. Stakic, by that decision, has been appointed to that duty. And this document was filed by the person in charge of the files of the health centre. What preceded Dr. Stakic's appointment was not up to me to check. It was not in the nature of my job, and I was not in the position to check it. As far as I know, this was a result of the interparty agreement which is a normal thing in the country where I come from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes, my question was only related to that if, for example, we would deem it necessary to revisit those documents as of 19 May, 1993, or 16th of July, 1998, you would not be prepared to immediately grant us copies or excerpts of this file? To be more concrete: You don't have any copies about this with you, be it here or in your hotel?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAVA DAKIC
utterances.text: No, no, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: It could have been of assistance, but you were not asked to do so. So please accept that I fully understand this. When did you hear for the first time ever the name of Dr. Stakic?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAVA DAKIC
utterances.text: The first time I saw Dr. Stakic was when he was still a young boy. He must have been 10 or 11 at the time. I worked as a paramedic at the time, and together with my senior colleague, I went to the territory where Dr. Stakic resided with his parents. But this was a very brief acquaintance. I was only aware of the fact that he was the eldest son in that family. My next information about Dr. Stakic dates back to the time when he was a medical student. Somehow, it was of some relevance to us to know who from the area where we worked went to the med school and whom we could expect to become a doctor. And then when he graduated from med school, he came to work to the same institution where I had already worked. From then onwards, we would meet in the street, in the workplace.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Did you ever meet him in the Municipal Assembly of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAVA DAKIC
utterances.text: I have never been to the building of the Municipal Assembly of Prijedor, at least not during the time where Dr. Stakic was there. We only go to that building if we have a valid reason.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The reason for my question was that just previously, you told us that you would meet also on the workplace.

utterances.speaker: BORISLAVA DAKIC
utterances.text: Maybe I haven't understood you properly, or maybe I'm not able to explain things properly. In Prijedor, you can meet people every day. You can meet the chief of the police, the president of the Municipal Assembly, or anybody else. But personally, I never went to the -- to the office of the president of the assembly, and I never met Dr. Stakic in his capacity as the president of the municipality. But his apartment is very close to the building where I work, and I could see Dr. Stakic a number of times on his way to work and from work. But even if I saw him, we didn't talk. We just exchanged a brief greeting, and that was it. I could also see Dr. Stakic driving in his car; I could see him in the park when he was playing with his children, with his son and his daughter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Could you explain exactly to us where this apartment was located.

utterances.speaker: BORISLAVA DAKIC
utterances.text: I believe that this is the apartment block M in Prijedor, and two blocks away from the health centre and the building of the occupational medicine department. These two buildings belong to the institution called the medical centre of Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Did you ever visit Dr. Stakic in his apartment?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAVA DAKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Turn to another subject: You told us in detail what was your work when working in Prijedor. I didn't really understand what was your work opposed to this when you had to go to Omarska. What was the work of a lawyer in the outpost in Omarska?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAVA DAKIC
utterances.text: No. In an outpatients' clinic the size of the clinic in Omarska, there's no real work for a lawyer. There are very few employees there. And a colleague of mine who had remained in Prijedor, she continued performing all the tasks and duties pertaining to that area. I've already told you winter was approaching. It was hard for me to travel. There was a need to look after the people in the hard times when there was a lack of all the bare necessities. This outpatients' clinic is some 25 to 30 kilometres away from Prijedor, and the director at the time sent me there. At the same time, there was not so much work in Prijedor for both me and my colleague to be working there full time as legal assistants.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Did you ever enter the facilities of Omarska camp at that time?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAVA DAKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Were ever doctors or anybody else from Omarska outpatients' clinic asked to give medical assistance for those needing medical assistance in Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAVA DAKIC
utterances.text: When I came from Prijedor to the outpatients' clinic in Omarska, there were no more detainees there. I believe that they had already been moved from that investigation centre to maybe Manjaca or to some other facility. I don't know. In any case, in June immediately after the conflict which took place on the 22nd, 23rd, and 24th of May, I was occasionally there in the Omarska outpatients' clinic, and during that period, I know that police members would ask doctors and paramedics from that outpatients' clinic to go there. Whenever they had such a request, a doctor would go and a few paramedics would go there. And from time to time, they would bring a person in need of assistance. At that time, I didn't enter these rooms, and the police members would only approach a doctor if they needed such assistance, nobody else. And it would be the doctor who would take a team of paramedics, and then they would go there if they thought that they could provide assistance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Another subject: The medical centre, did this medical centre have an additional name?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAVA DAKIC
utterances.text: Dr. Mladen Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I ask the usher, please, to present to the witness Exhibit S382 and at the same time S381-1 and -2. If this document could be immediately placed on the ELMO for a better understanding of all the participants. May I ask you, and as a lawyer, you know what your obligation is Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. as a witness, have you ever seen this list or a similar list?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAVA DAKIC
utterances.text: I've seen similar lists, but this one I can't be sure that I have seen it, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Acting as a lawyer there, was it part of your duty to check whether or not the legal prerequisites were met to dismiss a person, and whether or not for this reason, a name could be entered into such a list?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAVA DAKIC
utterances.text: In that period, these were not my duties. These were not the duties that I discharged. But I believe that it was checked whether the necessary prerequisites were met for somebody to be dismissed. I did not participate in putting these lists together, and I also didn't participate in drafting dismissal documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Do you know where the originals of these documents are in this period of time, in this moment? Do you have them still in Prijedor with you?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAVA DAKIC
utterances.text: I don't know where the originals are. Judging by the names on this list, I can conclude that these are all employees of the general hospital in Prijedor. Whether there are the originals of these lists in the general hospital or not, I wouldn't be able to tell you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Did you ever go through -- I don't want to confront you with all the lists we have available here. Did you ever go as a lawyer through these lists, and did you ever think about the reasons behind these lists?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAVA DAKIC
utterances.text: I have never looked at the lists. During 1992 and all the years thereafter, I have often thought about these events, and I have always wondered what has happened to us? Why has it happened to us? And did it really have to happen?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Could you please have a look on the second page of Document S381-1. You can see a signature or paraph of a signature of the document --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. As I mentioned in Court the other day, I do have the originals of Exhibit 381-1 and -2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: First, can you identify by this copy whose signature or paraph we can see beyond number 63, a human being, Emir Henic?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAVA DAKIC
utterances.text: No. I don't know whether this is a bad copy of the original. But in any case, in this document, I can't see --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So may I ask the Prosecution --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Usher, could you please pass these to the Judges, first. Your Honour, I showed them to Defence counsel when I raised the matter in Court that I had the originals.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: You may have a look on all the four pages, and then please tell us whether you identify either a signature or the handwriting you can find on the documents. And in order to save time, may already Document S386 be provided.

utterances.speaker: BORISLAVA DAKIC
utterances.text: No, I can't recognise the signature. However, speaking from the experience in the Mladen Stojanovic medical centre, it was not customary to compile such documents. Every document was letterheaded with Dr. Stojanovic medical centre, and the document had to contain the number and the date. And at the end of every document, there should have been a typed name of the person who signed the document and the position or title. As I don't see any of those here, I can only conclude or maybe guess that this was just a draft or a working material. In any case, this was not a valid final document. For a document to be valid, it had to contain the number, date, and it had to contain a typed-out name of the person who issued the document together with that person's title or position, be it the director or the medical technician or whoever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes. Recalling your answer, may you please have a look on Document 386 in the B/C/S version immediately on the ELMO, please. Do you know who drafted this document and who is responsible for this document?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAVA DAKIC
utterances.text: Everything is self-explanatory. This was compiled by Sikman, Ranko, the acting director of the medical centre, but his signature is missing. That means that it was pursuant to his order that the document was drafted, but for a document to be valid and enforced, it should have been signed by him. Maybe the signature is just not visible. Maybe this is a bad copy. In any case, I do not see any signatures on this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: We don't see either. Was it the custom when there were, as we can see here, five copies prepared that all the five copies and the original were signed by Mr. Sikman?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAVA DAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Is it -- please, you're a lawyer. Is it your testimony that all the copies ever were signed by Mr. Sikman in person?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAVA DAKIC
utterances.text: They should have been in accordance with the rules. All copies of a document had to be signed in handwriting. Whether he personally signed this one, I don't know. But here, I see that he didn't. Whether this document was applied and acted upon the way it was unsigned, I don't know. But in accordance with the regulations, all copies, regardless of their number, should have been signed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I'm afraid we can't conclude your testimony today because, no doubt, it's the right for the Defence to have some additional questions. And I think --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I need two minutes only, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Two minutes. Any questions from your side? There are a number of remaining questions, so unfortunately, we have to proceed tomorrow morning at 9.00. The trial stays adjourned until tomorrow, 9.00.
